mcq.questionText: Which command sequence correctly sets the global user name and email for Git and then verifies the configuration?
options: git config --global user.name "Alice" && git config --global user.email "alice@example.com" && git config --list
git config --system user.name "Alice" && git config --system user.email "alice@example.com" && git config --list
git config --global user.name "Alice" && git config --global user.email "alice@example.com" && git log
mcq.correctAnswer: git config --global user.name "Alice" && git config --global user.email "alice@example.com" && git config --list
mcq.explanation: The required steps are to set both user.name and user.email with the --global flag and then display all configuration values using git config --list. Using --system sets system-wide values, git log does not verify config, and omitting the email leaves the configuration incomplete.
